key_insight: Time-lagged cross-correlation (TCC) ranks existing flow modes by their association with a target observable, revealing structures that global-contribution rankings can miss.
engineering_relevance: Engineers can identify flow structures associated with specific force signals while comparing different observables within the same modal expansion.
method: Start with a fixed DMD or POD expansion, preserving spatial modes and temporal coefficients.
Rank mode groups by the mean squared norm of their cross-responses with a target observable over a lag window.
Select target-related structures without constructing a new modal basis.
evidence_signal: Tests recovered three low-contribution synthetic target structures with 2.15% target-subfield reconstruction error and identified observable-specific structures in cylinder-wake and cavity flows.
watch_item: Benefits from lag aggregation depend on the cross-response distribution and lag-window selection.
paper_title: Extracting target-related flow structures using a time-lagged cross-correlation ranking criterion
